script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union for Monday, November 16. Here is the week's news.

Lake Elmo's Planning Commission held a public hearing Monday on the city's 2027 to 2036 Capital Improvement Plan. The hearing was at 6:30 in the evening at Lake Elmo City Hall, 3880 Laverne Avenue North. Specific project lists or dollar figures were not in the notice.

Oakdale's council met Tuesday night on claims of two million eight hundred thirty-eight thousand five hundred sixty-three dollars and fifteen cents and a feasibility study for street reconstruction and overlay work. The claims cover October 28 through November 10. An agreement with SEH Inc. for the feasibility report is not to exceed forty-four thousand one hundred twelve dollars. From the October 27 workshop, proposed 2027 utility rates would raise a small residential bill by two dollars and sixty-four cents a month and a large residential bill by eight dollars and forty-eight cents a month. A large commercial customer with a 3-inch meter would see one hundred one dollars and twenty-four cents more a month. The packet notes city costs for the County Highway 13 project in a range around two hundred ninety-three thousand to five hundred thousand dollars. Street projects in the capital plan are listed at six point two million for reconstruction and two point six two million for overlay. The council also canvassed the November 3 general election returns and considered a resolution of support for the County Highway 13 improvement project. The meeting was at 7 at the Discovery Center, 4444 Hadley Avenue North.

Washington County commissioners met Tuesday morning on a public hearing for fee schedule revisions and on consent items that include a seventy-five thousand dollar amendment for homeless prevention, a three hundred thirty thousand dollar homecare software contract, a nine hundred ninety-five thousand nine hundred fifty-six dollar waste reduction grant, and three hundred eighty-six thousand five hundred ninety-eight dollars for intersection design. The board also heard an update on the election and the Land and Water Legacy Referendum and considered a resolution setting a process for any future look at automated license plate readers. A closed session reviewed a new appraisal of Phase II and Phase III of the Kelley Land and Cattle property for Big Marine Park Reserve. The agenda listed a purchase of 15085 62nd Street in Oak Park Heights for the Government Center Campus; the amount was not stated then. The meeting started at 9 a.m.

Washington County board adopted a resolution November 10 to buy the property at 15085 62nd Street in Oak Park Heights for three hundred fifty-seven thousand seven hundred dollars. The purchase adds the land to the Washington County Government Center Campus in Stillwater. The campus includes the Government Center, Law Enforcement Center, Courthouse, Emergency Housing Services Building, and parking ramp. The county has bought adjacent properties over the years as they became available. The board reviewed the proposed buy in closed session on September 15. It determined the property would provide long-term value by supporting future growth of the campus. The county and the property owners agreed on the price after negotiations.

Stillwater’s Heritage Preservation Commission met November 12 on a re-roof proposal for the Warden’s House Museum at 602 Main Street North and a historic interpretive signage project. The agenda listed a design review for the museum re-roof under new business. A workshop on the Historic Interpretive Signage Project was also listed.

Oakdale's Environmental Management Commission meets Monday night to hear a county climate action plan and review its 2027 work plan. Joe Ayers-Johnson and Macklyn Hutchison will present the Washington County Climate Action Plan in open forum. The commission will discuss the draft 2027 work plan. The 2026 city-wide cleanup recycled 97 percent of materials, with more mattresses, appliances, tires, electronics, and trash than in 2025. The meeting is at 7 p.m. at the Discovery Center, 4444 Hadley Avenue North.

Times and documents are in the show notes.
